1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-command-deck
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The Command Deck is the customer-facing front end of the Daliesk agent enterprise: 147 defined agents, the workflows between them, the live activity of a harness run, and a code-safety review placed on the target repository's own code.
6	
7	It is a Next.js 14 application (App Router, React 18) whose three scenes are three.js through `@react-three/fiber`. It reads one HTTP feed and, when that feed does not answer, replays the fixtures committed beside it — so the deck is fully usable, and demonstrable, with no server running and no API key.
8	
9	## Run it
10	
11	Run the first from the repository root; the second is `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck dev` under another name.
12	
13	```sh
14	pnpm install
15	pnpm run deck
16	```
17	
18	The deck serves on `http://localhost:3000`. Point it at a live feed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL`; the default is `http://localhost:4711`.
19	
20	The second line is the production build and the server over it; the third regenerates `fixtures/`.
21	
22	```sh
23	NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL=http://localhost:4711 pnpm run deck
24	pnpm --dir apps/command-deck build && pnpm --dir apps/command-deck start
25	pnpm --dir apps/command-deck fixtures
26	```
27	
28	## The three views
29	
30	| Key | View | What it shows |
31	| --- | --- | --- |
32	| `1` | **Enterprise** (`/`) | Every defined agent as a node, clustered by division, edges for the delegations, verifications and judgements between them. A node pulses while its agent acts; a ring bursts where a certificate is issued. Clicking one opens its role, model route, preset, skills, tools, source file, and its own events in the run being followed. |
33	| `2` | **Process** (`/process`) | The program pipeline — departments, Verification, Judging, Integration — with every logged event travelling as a comet from its stage to the next. A timeline scrubber replays the run from any point; `Head` returns to live. |
34	| `3` | **Code safety** (`/safety`) | The reviewed repository as a code city: directories are districts, files are blocks scaled by size and coloured by language, and every finding is a marker standing on the line of code that carries it. The panel holds the findings table with severity, department and CWE filters, the certificate with its counts and its unverified list, the bilingual report, downloads, and the form that starts a new review. |
35	
36	`Esc` clears the selection. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` turns off the auto-orbit, the pulsing and the chromatic aberration, and holds bloom at a constant intensity.
37	
38	![The enterprise view: 147 agents in ten division clusters](docs/enterprise.png)
39	
40	![The process view: departments, verification, judging and integration](docs/process.png)
41	
42	![The code-safety view: the code city with findings on their files](docs/safety.png)
43	
44	## The feed contract
45	
46	The deck reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL` (default `http://localhost:4711`) and expects these paths. The feed server itself is not in this package.
47	
48	| Path | Answer |
49	| --- | --- |
50	| `GET /roster` | `{ generatedAt, counts: { defined, active }, divisions[], agents[], edges[] }` — the 147 agents, their divisions and their relationships. |
51	| `GET /runs` | `[{ id, kind, name, startedAt, endedAt?, status, path }]` for every `program`, `fleet`, `experiment` and `code-safety` run. |
52	| `GET /runs/:id/events` | Server-Sent Events. Each `data:` frame is one `{ ts, seq, agentId, sessionId, kind, label, detail?, severity?, file?, line? }`. The stream replays history and then stays open. |
53	| `GET /safety/:id` | `{ target, departments, findings, certificate, report }` for one code-safety review. |
54	| `POST /safety` | `{ target, model? }` starts a review and answers `{ id }`; the deck then follows that run live. `target` is an absolute path on the feed's machine and `model` is `sonnet` or `opus`, the names `pnpm run code-safety -- --model` accepts; the form opens on the loaded review's own target. |
55	
56	Every field is typed in [`deck/contract.ts`](deck/contract.ts), which is the one place the contract is written down. `seq` is what the client deduplicates on, so a reconnection that replays history delivers nothing twice.
57	
58	Two deck-side rules are worth knowing because the feed does not carry them. A finding's owning department is derived from its CWE through the table in [`deck/departments.ts`](deck/departments.ts), since the feed reports per-department totals but places no department on the finding itself. A finding counts as verified unless the certificate's `unverified` list names it.
59	
60	## Replay: what happens with no feed
61	
62	On load the deck sends one `GET /roster` to the configured feed with a 5-second timeout. Any failure — connection refused, timeout, non-2xx, a blocked cross-origin request — selects replay mode, and every later read goes to the deck's own routes under `/api/fixtures`, which serve the same paths with the same payloads. The header badge reads `REPLAY` instead of `LIVE`, the status footer names the feed it could not reach, and each view carries a standing **Example data** notice, so a screenshot cannot be mistaken for a live run.
63	
64	The replayed event stream is paced rather than dumped: the route delivers the first 60% of the recording immediately as history, then releases the rest a frame at a time, then holds the connection open. A keyless demo therefore shows an enterprise at work rather than a static file.
65	
66	`POST /safety` in replay mode reopens the recorded review instead of starting a new one, and says so under the form.
67	
68	## The fixtures
69	
70	`fixtures/` is generated by `scripts/generate-fixtures.ts` from one seeded PRNG, so regenerating produces byte-identical files.
71	
72	- `fixtures/roster.json` — 147 agents across ten divisions (Harness Core, Proving Ground, Verification, Judging, Curation and Data, Program Departments, Code Safety with its six departments, Knowledge, Governance, Observatory) and 424 relationships. The division sizes and the members are written down in `scripts/roster-source.ts`.
73	- `fixtures/runs.json` — one code-safety run, one program, one fleet shift, one paired experiment.
74	- `fixtures/events/<run>.jsonl` — the recorded streams; the code-safety run holds just over three hundred events, from the opening directive through six departments sweeping the tree in parallel, findings landing, the verifier re-reading each one at its line, judging, integration, and the certificate.
75	- `fixtures/safety/<run>.json` — the review: 34 files, 26 findings, the department roll-up, the certificate with its two named unverified findings, and the report in French and English.
76	
77	The code-safety findings are not invented. Eighteen of the twenty-six are read from [`data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json`](../../data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json), this repository's own ground truth for OWASP NodeGoat at revision `c5cb68a`, with their real CWE, file and line. The remaining eight are departmental output beyond that ground truth and carry lower confidence to match.
78	
79	## Layout
80	
81	| Directory | Holds |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| `app/` | The routes, and the fixture endpoints under `app/api/fixtures/`. |
84	| `components/` | The shell, and one folder per view; everything touching three.js is a Client Component. |
85	| `deck/` | The contract, the feed client, the event stream, the store, the layouts, the palette. |
86	| `fixtures/` | The committed replay data. |
87	| `scripts/` | The fixture generator and its roster source. |
88	| `docs/` | The screenshots above. |
89	
90	The shell (`app/layout.tsx`) is a Server Component. Each scene is loaded through `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`, because three.js reaches for a WebGL context on mount.
91	
92	## Limitations
93	
94	The deck reads; it never writes to a repository and never runs a review itself — `POST /safety` asks the feed to. A live feed on another origin must send CORS headers the browser accepts, or the deck falls back to replay. The scenes need WebGL 2; there is no 2D fallback. The code city places a finding only when the target's file list contains its `file`, and a finding on a file the feed did not report is listed in the table but carries no marker.
95

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

176	  // Recentre on the node cloud's own centroid: cluster sizes differ, so the
177	  // shell's geometric centre is not where the graph actually sits, and the
178	  // camera frames what it is told is the origin.
179	  const centroid = nodes.reduce(
180	    (acc, node) => ({ x: acc.x + node.x, y: acc.y + node.y, z: acc.z + node.z }),
181	    { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 },
182	  )
183	  centroid.x /= nodes.length
184	  centroid.y /= nodes.length
185	  centroid.z /= nodes.length
186	  for (const node of nodes) {
187	    node.x -= centroid.x
188	    node.y -= centroid.y
189	    node.z -= centroid.z
190	  }
191	
192	  // A label sits outside its own cloud, pushed radially away from the graph
193	  // centre by the cluster's own radius, so it never lands on top of a node.
194	  const clusters: GraphCluster[] = roster.divisions.map((entry) => {
195	    const members = nodes.filter(node => node.division === entry.id)
196	    const count = Math.max(members.length, 1)
197	    const centre = members.reduce(
198	      (acc, node) => ({ x: acc.x + node.x, y: acc.y + node.y, z: acc.z + node.z }),
199	      { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 },
200	    )
201	    centre.x /= count
202	    centre.y /= count
203	    centre.z /= count
204	    const radius = members.reduce((acc, node) => Math.max(
205	      acc,
206	      Math.hypot(node.x - centre.x, node.y - centre.y, node.z - centre.z),
207	    ), 6)
208	    const distance = Math.hypot(centre.x, centre.y, centre.z) || 1
209	    const push = (radius + 7) / distance
210	    return {
211	      id: entry.id,
212	      name: entry.name,
213	      x: centre.x * (1 + push),
214	      y: (centre.y * (1 + push)) + 4,
215	      z: centre.z * (1 + push),
216	      count: members.length,
217	    }
218	  })
219	
220	  const extent = nodes.reduce(
221	    (acc, node) => Math.max(acc, Math.sqrt((node.x * node.x) + (node.y * node.y) + (node.z * node.z))),
222	    1,
223	  )
224	
225	  return { nodes, clusters, index, extent }
226	}

1	/**
2	 * The deck's single client store.
3	 *
4	 * Two kinds of state live here. React state (roster, runs, events, selection)
5	 * drives rendering. Frame state — `activity` and `bursts` — is mutated in
6	 * place and read from `useFrame`, because a sixty-times-a-second render pass
7	 * must not go through React at all.
8	 */
9	
10	'use client'
11	
12	import { create } from 'zustand'
13	import type { Roster, Run, RunEvent, SafetyReview } from './contract.ts'
14	import { getRoster, getRuns, getSafety, resolveFeed, type FeedSource } from './feed.ts'
15	import { subscribeRun, type StreamState } from './stream.ts'
16	
17	/** How many events one run keeps in memory; older frames fall off the head. */
18	const EVENT_WINDOW = 4_000
19	
20	/** How often a live deck re-reads the run list and a running review's detail. */
21	const REFRESH_MS = 10_000
22	
23	/** A certificate burst waiting to be drawn once, then dropped. */
24	interface Burst {
25	  agentId: string
26	  at: number
27	}
28	
29	/** Everything the deck holds for one session. */
30	export interface DeckState {
31	  source: FeedSource | undefined
32	  streamState: StreamState
33	  roster: Roster | undefined
34	  runs: Run[]
35	  selectedRunId: string | undefined
36	  events: RunEvent[]
37	  safety: SafetyReview | undefined
38	  safetyRunId: string | undefined
39	  selectedAgentId: string | undefined
40	  selectedFindingId: string | undefined
41	  error: string | undefined
42	  booted: boolean
43	  /** Timeline position as a sequence number; `undefined` follows the head. */
44	  cursor: number | undefined
45	  /** Last activity timestamp per agent, in `performance.now()` milliseconds. */
46	  activity: Map<string, number>
47	  /** Certificate bursts the enterprise scene has not drawn yet. */
48	  bursts: Burst[]
49	  boot: () => Promise<void>
50	  selectRun: (id: string) => void
51	  /** List a run the feed does not report yet, such as a review this deck just started. */
52	  addRun: (run: Run) => void
53	  /** Re-read the run list and, while the followed review is still running, its detail. */
54	  refresh: () => Promise<void>
55	  selectAgent: (id: string | undefined) => void
56	  selectFinding: (id: string | undefined) => void
57	  setCursor: (seq: number | undefined) => void
58	  /** Load a review's detail; `force` re-reads one already loaded. */
59	  loadSafety: (id: string, force?: boolean) => Promise<void>
60	}
61	
62	let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined
63	
64	/**
65	 * Append one event to the window, dropping the oldest frames past the cap.
66	 * @param events - The current window.
67	 * @param event - The frame to append.
68	 * @returns The new window.
69	 */
70	function appendEvent(events: RunEvent[], event: RunEvent): RunEvent[] {
71	  const next = [...events, event]
72	  return next.length > EVENT_WINDOW ? next.slice(next.length - EVENT_WINDOW) : next
73	}
74	
75	export const useDeck = create<DeckState>((set, get) => ({
76	  source: undefined,
77	  streamState: 'idle',
78	  roster: undefined,
79	  runs: [],
80	  selectedRunId: undefined,
81	  events: [],
82	  safety: undefined,
83	  safetyRunId: undefined,
84	  selectedAgentId: undefined,
85	  selectedFindingId: undefined,
86	  error: undefined,
87	  booted: false,
88	  cursor: undefined,
89	  activity: new Map<string, number>(),
90	  bursts: [],
91	
92	  boot: async () => {
93	    if (get().booted) return
94	    set({ booted: true })
95	    const source = await resolveFeed()
96	    set({ source })
97	    try {
98	      const [roster, runs] = await Promise.all([getRoster(source.base), getRuns(source.base)])
99	      set({ roster, runs })
100	      const safetyRun = runs.find(run => run.kind === 'code-safety') ?? runs[0]
101	      if (safetyRun !== undefined) get().selectRun(safetyRun.id)
102	    } catch (error) {
103	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
104	    }
105	    // Replay is a fixed record; only a live feed changes underneath the deck.
106	    if (source.mode === 'live') setInterval(() => { void get().refresh() }, REFRESH_MS)
107	  },
108	
109	  addRun: (run) => {
110	    set(state => (state.runs.some(entry => entry.id === run.id) ? {} : { runs: [run, ...state.runs] }))
111	  },
112	
113	  refresh: async () => {
114	    const { source, runs: known, selectedRunId } = get()
115	    if (source === undefined) return
116	    try {
117	      const listed = await getRuns(source.base)
118	      // A review this deck started stays listed until the feed reports it.
119	      const pending = known.filter(run => !listed.some(entry => entry.id === run.id))
120	      set({ runs: [...pending, ...listed] })
121	      const selected = [...pending, ...listed].find(run => run.id === selectedRunId)
122	      if (selected?.kind === 'code-safety' && (selected.status === 'running' || get().safetyRunId !== selected.id)) {
123	        await get().loadSafety(selected.id, true)
124	      }
125	    } catch (error) {
126	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
127	    }
128	  },
129	
130	  selectRun: (id) => {
131	    const source = get().source
132	    if (source === undefined || get().selectedRunId === id) return
133	    unsubscribe?.()
134	    set({ selectedRunId: id, events: [], cursor: undefined })
135	    const { activity } = get()
136	    activity.clear()
137	    unsubscribe = subscribeRun(source.base, id, {
138	      onState: state => set({ streamState: state }),
139	      onEvent: (event) => {
140	        get().activity.set(event.agentId, performance.now())
141	        if (event.kind === 'certificate') {
142	          get().bursts.push({ agentId: event.agentId, at: performance.now() })
143	        }
144	        set(state => ({ events: appendEvent(state.events, event) }))
145	      },
146	    })
147	    const run = get().runs.find(entry => entry.id === id)
148	    if (run?.kind === 'code-safety') void get().loadSafety(id)
149	  },
150	
151	  selectAgent: id => set({ selectedAgentId: id }),
152	  selectFinding: id => set({ selectedFindingId: id }),
153	  setCursor: seq => set({ cursor: seq }),
154	
155	  loadSafety: async (id, force = false) => {
156	    const source = get().source
157	    if (source === undefined || (!force && get().safetyRunId === id)) return
158	    try {
159	      // No finding is preselected: the view opens on the whole city, and the
160	      // camera only flies in once a reviewer picks one. A re-read keeps the
161	      // selection when the finding is still there.
162	      const safety = await getSafety(source.base, id)
163	      const selectedFindingId = get().selectedFindingId
164	      const kept = force && safety.findings.some(finding => finding.id === selectedFindingId) ? selectedFindingId : undefined
165	      set({ safety, safetyRunId: id, selectedFindingId: kept, error: undefined })
166	    } catch (error) {
167	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
168	    }
169	  },
170	}))
171	
172	/**
173	 * The events the timeline currently admits.
174	 * @param events - The full window.
175	 * @param cursor - Sequence cap, or `undefined` to follow the head.
176	 * @returns Events up to and including the cursor.
177	 */
178	export function eventsUpTo(events: readonly RunEvent[], cursor: number | undefined): RunEvent[] {
179	  if (cursor === undefined) return [...events]
180	  return events.filter(event => event.seq <= cursor)
181	}

3	import { Canvas } from '@react-three/fiber'
4	import { Bloom, ChromaticAberration, EffectComposer, Vignette } from '@react-three/postprocessing'
5	import { BlendFunction } from 'postprocessing'
6	import { useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react'

9	
10	/** Camera placement one stage asks for. */
11	export interface StageCamera {
12	  position: [number, number, number]
13	  fov: number
14	}

16	/**
17	 * The shared three.js stage: one canvas, one colour grade.
18	 *
19	 * Every view renders through the same composer so the three scenes read as one
20	 * instrument. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the grade loses its chromatic
21	 * aberration and holds bloom at a lower constant intensity, because the effect
22	 * that sells the image at rest is also the one that shimmers.
23	 * @param props - Camera placement and the scene contents.
24	 * @returns The canvas.
25	 */
26	export function Stage({
27	  camera,
28	  children,
29	  fogNear = 120,
30	  fogFar = 420,
31	}: {
32	  camera: StageCamera
33	  children: ReactNode
34	  fogNear?: number
35	  fogFar?: number
36	}): ReactNode {
37	  const reduced = usePrefersReducedMotion()
38	  const aberration = useMemo(() => new Vector2(0.00055, 0.0009), [])
39	
40	  return (
41	    <Canvas
42	      dpr={[1, 1.75]}
43	      gl={{ antialias: false, alpha: false, powerPreference: 'high-performance' }}
44	      camera={{ position: camera.position, fov: camera.fov, near: 0.5, far: 2_000 }}
45	      frameloop="always"
46	    >
47	      <color attach="background" args={['#04060b']} />
48	      <fog attach="fog" args={['#04060b', fogNear, fogFar]} />
49	
50	      <ambientLight intensity={0.55} />
51	      <directionalLight position={[40, 90, 60]} intensity={0.9} color="#bcd6ff" />
52	      <directionalLight position={[-60, -30, -40]} intensity={0.35} color="#7b6bff" />
53	
54	      {children}
55	
56	      <EffectComposer multisampling={0} enableNormalPass={false}>
57	        <Bloom
58	          intensity={reduced ? 0.7 : 1.35}
59	          luminanceThreshold={0.1}
60	          luminanceSmoothing={0.42}
61	          mipmapBlur
62	          radius={0.78}
63	        />
64	        {reduced ? <></> : (
65	          <ChromaticAberration
66	            blendFunction={BlendFunction.NORMAL}
67	            offset={aberration}
68	            radialModulation
69	            modulationOffset={0.35}
70	          />
71	        )}
72	        <Vignette offset={0.2} darkness={0.82} eskil={false} blendFunction={BlendFunction.NORMAL} />
73	      </EffectComposer>
74	    </Canvas>
75	  )
76	}

3	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
4	
5	/**
6	 * Whether the viewer asked for reduced motion.
7	 *
8	 * The deck honours it by dropping auto-orbit, pulsing and chromatic
9	 * aberration, and by holding bloom at a constant intensity. The initial value
10	 * is `false` so the server render and the first client render agree; the media
11	 * query resolves immediately afterwards.
12	 * @returns `true` once `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches.
13	 */
14	export function usePrefersReducedMotion(): boolean {
15	  const [reduced, setReduced] = useState(false)
16	
17	  useEffect(() => {
18	    const query = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')
19	    setReduced(query.matches)
20	    const onChange = (event: MediaQueryListEvent): void => setReduced(event.matches)
21	    query.addEventListener('change', onChange)
22	    return () => query.removeEventListener('change', onChange)
23	  }, [])
24	
25	  return reduced
26	}

1	/**
2	 * The run event stream client.
3	 *
4	 * `GET /runs/:id/events` replays history and then stays open, so a reconnect
5	 * receives frames the deck already holds. Every frame carries a monotonic
6	 * `seq`, which is what deduplication keys on: the caller's `onEvent` sees each
7	 * sequence number exactly once for the life of the subscription, across any
8	 * number of reconnections.
9	 */
10	
11	import type { RunEvent } from './contract.ts'
12	
13	/** Connection state the status bar reports. */
14	export type StreamState = 'idle' | 'connecting' | 'open' | 'retrying' | 'closed'
15	
16	/** Callbacks a subscription reports through. */
17	export interface StreamHandlers {
18	  onEvent: (event: RunEvent) => void
19	  onState: (state: StreamState) => void
20	}
21	
22	/** Reconnection backoff, in milliseconds, indexed by consecutive failure count. */
23	const BACKOFF_MS = [800, 1_600, 3_200, 6_400, 10_000] as const
24	
25	/**
26	 * Parse one `data:` frame.
27	 * @param data - The frame's payload.
28	 * @returns The event, or `undefined` when the frame is not a usable event.
29	 */
30	function parseFrame(data: string): RunEvent | undefined {
31	  let value: unknown
32	  try {
33	    value = JSON.parse(data)
34	  } catch {
35	    // A truncated or heartbeat frame is not an error: the stream stays open and
36	    // the next frame carries the next sequence number.
37	    return undefined
38	  }
39	  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined
40	  const event = value as Partial<RunEvent>
41	  if (typeof event.seq !== 'number' || typeof event.kind !== 'string' || typeof event.agentId !== 'string') {
42	    return undefined
43	  }
44	  return event as RunEvent
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * Subscribe to one run's events until the returned disposer is called.
49	 *
50	 * The subscription owns its own `EventSource`: `EventSource` reconnects on its
51	 * own after a network drop, and this wrapper additionally reopens after an
52	 * error that closed the source for good, with bounded backoff.
53	 * @param base - Base URL from `resolveFeed`.
54	 * @param runId - The run to follow.
55	 * @param handlers - Event and state callbacks.
56	 * @returns A disposer that closes the stream and stops any pending retry.
57	 */
58	export function subscribeRun(base: string, runId: string, handlers: StreamHandlers): () => void {
59	  const url = `${base}/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}/events`
60	  const seen = new Set<number>()
61	  let source: EventSource | undefined
62	  let retry: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
63	  let failures = 0
64	  let disposed = false
65	
66	  const open = (): void => {
67	    if (disposed) return
68	    handlers.onState(failures === 0 ? 'connecting' : 'retrying')
69	    const next = new EventSource(url)
70	    source = next
71	
72	    next.onopen = () => {
73	      failures = 0
74	      handlers.onState('open')
75	    }
76	
77	    next.onmessage = (message: MessageEvent<string>) => {
78	      const event = parseFrame(message.data)
79	      if (event === undefined || seen.has(event.seq)) return
80	      seen.add(event.seq)
81	      handlers.onEvent(event)
82	    }
83	
84	    next.onerror = () => {
85	      // EventSource retries a dropped connection itself and only reports
86	      // CLOSED when it has given up; anything else is a transient reconnect.
87	      if (next.readyState !== EventSource.CLOSED) {
88	        handlers.onState('retrying')
89	        return
90	      }
91	      next.close()
92	      if (disposed) return
93	      const wait = BACKOFF_MS[Math.min(failures, BACKOFF_MS.length - 1)] ?? 10_000
94	      failures += 1
95	      handlers.onState('retrying')
96	      retry = setTimeout(open, wait)
97	    }
98	  }
99	
100	  open()
101	
102	  return () => {
103	    disposed = true
104	    if (retry !== undefined) clearTimeout(retry)
105	    source?.close()
106	    handlers.onState('closed')
107	  }
108	}

'use client'

import { useMemo, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import type { Roster } from '@/deck/contract'
import { layoutRoster } from '@/deck/layout-enterprise'
import { Stage } from '@/components/three/Stage'
import { AgentGraph } from './AgentGraph'
import { CameraRig } from './CameraRig'
import { CertificateBursts } from './CertificateBursts'
import { Constellations } from './Constellations'
import { GraphEdges } from './GraphEdges'

/**
 * The enterprise scene: ten constellations, the agents inside them, the
 * relationships between them, and the traffic the followed run puts on those
 * relationships.
 *
 * The layers are drawn back to front — nebulae, edges and their traffic,
 * agents, certificate bursts — and each one is a single instanced or
 * point-based draw over the whole roster.
 * @param props - The roster to draw.
 * @returns The canvas and its contents.
 */
export function EnterpriseStage({ roster }: { roster: Roster }): ReactNode {
  const layout = useMemo(() => layoutRoster(roster), [roster])

  return (
    <Stage camera={{ position: [0, layout.extent * 0.26, layout.extent * 2.2], fov: 44 }} fogNear={210} fogFar={720}>
      <Constellations roster={roster} layout={layout} />
      <GraphEdges roster={roster} layout={layout} />
      <AgentGraph roster={roster} layout={layout} />
      <CertificateBursts layout={layout} />
      <CameraRig layout={layout} />
    </Stage>
  )
}

deck(enterprise): living edges, agent bodies, timed camera

The scene moves out of one file into one file per layer, and each layer
now reads the run rather than the clock.

The camera opens far out and high above the graph and eases down into
the resting orbit over two and a half seconds, then keeps the slow
auto-orbit it had; selecting an agent flies to it in one second and two
tenths along the direction the viewer was already looking from, and Esc
flies back. Every move is a timed cubic ease, so it lands on its beat
instead of drifting with the frame rate.

Traffic particles ride an edge from its source to its target, coloured
by the relationship's kind, but only while one of its two agents has
acted inside the activity window. With nothing live nothing flows and
the edge layer breathes in brightness on a ten-second cycle, so an idle
enterprise looks idle without looking dead.

Agents gain bodies: a softer halo behind each core, a thin tilted ring
that turns around an agent while it is working, a warm rim on a
certified agent and a dim red one on a failed agent. Selecting an agent
drops every unrelated node and edge to three tenths, holds its
neighbours in between, and burns its own edges at full.

Under prefers-reduced-motion the deck opens at rest, nothing flows,
nothing pulses, and selection cuts straight to its shot.

15	/** How many certificate bursts can be on screen at once. */
16	const BURST_POOL = 8
17	
18	/** Lifetime of one certificate burst, in milliseconds. */
19	const BURST_MS = 1_300
20	
21	/** One live certificate burst. */
22	interface LiveBurst {
23	  position: Vector3
24	  started: number
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * Expanding rings where a certificate was just issued.
29	 * @param props - The computed layout, used to place each burst on its agent.
30	 * @returns The burst rings.
31	 */
32	function CertificateBursts({ layout }: { layout: GraphLayout }): ReactNode {
33	  const bursts = useDeck(state => state.bursts)
34	  const live = useRef<LiveBurst[]>([])
35	  const rings = useRef<(Mesh | null)[]>([])
36	  const { camera } = useThree()
37	
38	  useFrame(() => {
39	    // Drain the store's queue: every burst is drawn once, then forgotten.
40	    while (bursts.length > 0) {
41	      const burst = bursts.shift()
42	      if (burst === undefined) break
43	      const node = layout.nodes[layout.index.get(burst.agentId) ?? -1]
44	      if (node === undefined) continue
45	      live.current.push({ position: new Vector3(node.x, node.y, node.z), started: performance.now() })
46	      if (live.current.length > BURST_POOL) live.current.shift()
47	    }
48	
49	    const now = performance.now()
50	    for (const [index, ring] of rings.current.entries()) {
51	      if (ring === null) continue
52	      const burst = live.current[index]
53	      if (burst === undefined) {
54	        ring.visible = false
55	        continue
56	      }
57	      const age = (now - burst.started) / BURST_MS
58	      if (age >= 1) {
59	        ring.visible = false
60	        continue
61	      }
62	      ring.visible = true
63	      ring.position.copy(burst.position)
64	      ring.quaternion.copy(camera.quaternion)
65	      ring.scale.setScalar(1.5 + (age * 13))
66	      const material = ring.material
67	      if (!Array.isArray(material) && 'opacity' in material) material.opacity = (1 - age) * 0.8
68	    }
69	
70	    live.current = live.current.filter(burst => now - burst.started < BURST_MS)
71	  })
72	
73	  return (
74	    <group>
75	      {Array.from({ length: BURST_POOL }, (_, index) => (
76	        <mesh
77	          key={index}
78	          ref={(mesh) => { rings.current[index] = mesh }}
79	          visible={false}
80	        >
81	          <ringGeometry args={[0.84, 1, 48]} />
82	          <meshBasicMaterial
83	            color="#49e0a6"
84	            transparent
85	            opacity={0}
86	            side={DoubleSide}
87	            blending={AdditiveBlending}
88	            depthWrite={false}
89	            toneMapped={false}
90	          />
91	        </mesh>
92	      ))}
93	    </group>
94	  )
95	}
96	
97	/**
98	 * The enterprise scene.
99	 * @param props - The roster to draw.
100	 * @returns The canvas and its contents.
101	 */
102	export function EnterpriseStage({ roster }: { roster: Roster }): ReactNode {
103	  const layout = useMemo(() => layoutRoster(roster), [roster])
104	
105	  return (
106	    <Stage camera={{ position: [0, layout.extent * 0.26, layout.extent * 2.2], fov: 44 }} fogNear={210} fogFar={720}>
107	      <Constellations roster={roster} layout={layout} />
108	      <GraphEdges roster={roster} layout={layout} />
109	      <AgentGraph roster={roster} layout={layout} />
110	      <CertificateBursts layout={layout} />
111	      <CameraRig layout={layout} />
112	    </Stage>
113	  )
114	}

attachment.snippet:
1	/**
2	 * The enterprise graph's 3D layout.
3	 *
4	 * The layout is computed once per roster and then cached: it is a force
5	 * relaxation, not an animation, so running it every frame would buy nothing
6	 * and cost the frame budget the scene needs. Division clusters are placed on a
7	 * fixed ring first, then nodes relax inside their cluster under edge springs
8	 * and local repulsion, which keeps each division readable as a body while the
9	 * cross-division edges still pull related agents towards each other.
10	 */
11	
12	import type { Roster } from './contract.ts'
13	
14	/** One node's resolved position and its cluster. */
15	interface GraphNode {
16	  id: string
17	  x: number
18	  y: number
19	  z: number
20	  division: string
21	}
22	
23	/** A division's cluster centre and label anchor. */
24	interface GraphCluster {
25	  id: string
26	  name: string
27	  x: number
28	  y: number
29	  z: number
30	  count: number
31	}
32	
33	/** The laid-out graph the scene renders. */
34	export interface GraphLayout {
35	  nodes: GraphNode[]
36	  clusters: GraphCluster[]
37	  /** Index of each node id in `nodes`, for edge and selection lookups. */
38	  index: Map<string, number>
39	  /** Radius of the sphere that contains every node, for camera framing. */
40	  extent: number
41	}
42	
43	/** Radius of the shell the division clusters sit on. */
44	const SHELL_RADIUS = 66
45	
46	/** How far the shell is flattened vertically, so the graph reads as a body. */
47	const SHELL_FLATTEN = 0.56
48	
49	/** Relaxation passes; enough for a stable picture, cheap enough to run on mount. */
50	const PASSES = 260
51	
52	/**
53	 * Deterministic 32-bit PRNG, so the same roster always lays out identically.
54	 * @param seed - Any 32-bit integer.
55	 * @returns A function returning the next float in `[0, 1)`.
56	 */

content.text:
The Enterprise view is rebuilt, committed, and verified. Final report below.

## Commits (worktree `agent-ae5919d091ab083a6`, oldest first)

| Hash | Subject |
| --- | --- |
| `752b293cf` | deck(enterprise): cluster centroids, radii and lifted labels |
| `bfd56b5e4` | deck(enterprise): living edges, agent bodies, timed camera |
| `d23f917f3` | deck(enterprise): divisions as constellations |
| `9f6ec369b` | deck(enterprise): a beam of light on every certificate |

`git log -1 --format='%ae %ce'` → `noreply@anthropic.com noreply@anthropic.com`. Working tree clean; nothing pushed.

## What changed, per file

`deck/layout-enterprise.ts` — `GraphCluster` now also carries the members' true centroid (`cx/cy/cz`) and `radius`; `GraphNode`/`GraphCluster` are exported. Label anchors sit further out and are lifted by a share of the cluster radius, so a division name clears its own cloud.

`components/enterprise/EnterpriseStage.tsx` — now only composition: nebulae → edges+traffic → agents → bursts → camera.

`components/enterprise/CameraRig.tsx` (new) — shots and timed flights. Opens at `(0.85, 1.35, 3.0) × extent` and eases (cubic in-out, 2.5 s) to the resting orbit; measured in-browser the camera goes distance 261 / height 104 → 170 / 20 in ~2.45 s. Selection flies in 1.2 s along the direction the viewer was already looking from (so the flight closes in on what was clicked rather than cutting through the cluster); Esc flies back the same way. Auto-orbit and damping unchanged, disabled during a flight; a drag cancels the flight and hands the camera over. Under reduced motion it opens at rest and selection cuts.

`components/enterprise/GraphEdges.tsx` (new) — the line layers plus `EdgeTraffic`: one Points layer of 320 particles over a preallocated pool (`Int32Array` edge, `Float32Array` progress/speed), advanced in `useFrame` with no per-frame allocation. An edge carries traffic only while `store.activity` says one of its endpoints acted within 5 s; the live set is recomputed on a 220 ms clock, at most 3 particles per edge, staggered entries, colour from `EDGE_COLOR`. With nothing live nothing flows and the edge layer breathes ±0.075 opacity on a ~10 s cycle.

`components/enterprise/AgentGraph.tsx` (new) — four layers over the roster: instanced cores, the softened halo Points layer, an instanced tilted orbital ring worn only while an agent is working (or roster status `active`), and an instanced camera-facing rim — warm on `certified`, dim red on `failed`. Selection weights (1 / 0.62 neighbour / 0.3 rest) are computed once per selection into a `Float32Array` and consumed by the frame loop; core and rim colours are written in a layout effect, not per frame. Hover label kept, now from the CSS module and clamped to the stage.

`components/enterprise/Constellations.tsx` (new) — an instanced, billboarded nebula per division tinted with the division colour, sized from the cluster radius, its brightness the share of that division's agents active inside the window; a leader-line layer from each label down to its centroid; the division labels themselves.

`components/enterprise/CertificateBursts.tsx` (new) — bursts as two instanced layers over a pool of eight: an expanding ring and a short vertical beam that turns on its own axis to face the camera, both fading through their instance colour under additive blending. Reduced motion holds size and cuts.

`components/enterprise/{arcs,activity,labels,sprites}.ts`, `labels.module.css` (new) — shared arc math (line layer and particles ride the same Bézier), the activity window helpers, the label clamp (an anchor outside the frame parks its label off-stage instead of stacking names on the header/panel edge), the nebula texture and beam geometry, and the label styles.

Panels untouched: `AgentPanel`/`OverviewPanel` still open on click and clear on Esc (verified in the screenshots).

## New interactions
Establishing shot on mount; click a node → 1.2 s flight, everything unrelated to 0.3, its own edges at full; Esc → flight back to rest; hover → name + role label; drag during any flight takes the camera over.

## Frame time (temporary `useFrame` probe, removed before the first commit)
Median of per-frame deltas over a rolling 120-frame window, headless Chromium + SwiftShader, dev build, live feed, three page loads each:

| Viewport | Before (`e793c2842`) | After | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 800×500 | 105.9 / 83.1 / **103.7** ms | 116.1 / 157.4 / **117.8** ms | **1.14×** |
| 1600×1000 | 348.7 / 423.7 / **348.7** ms | 563.6 / 402.2 / **402.2** ms | **1.15×** |

Within the 1.5× budget. Caveat: software WebGL on a host shared with three other agents, so the numbers are fill-bound and noisy in absolute terms; the added cost is mostly the ten large additive nebula quads, not geometry. Draw calls for the whole scene: 11 (nebulae, edges, selected edges, traffic, leader lines, cores, halos, orbital rings, rims, burst rings, burst beams), each one layer over the whole roster. No React state updates per frame.

## Screenshots
Under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-deepseek-harness/f53f80cc-1f77-5d02-a862-99d59ffabdce/scratchpad/ent/`:
- before, live: `before-live/ent-rest.png` · before, replay: `before/before-replay-rest.png`
- after, live: `after/after-live-flow.png` (traffic from the code-safety lead to Program Departments), `after/after-live-rest.png`, `after/after-live-selected.png`
- after, replay (424 edges): `after/after-replay-flow.png`
- after, reduced motion: `after/rm-after-reduced-motion.png`
- mid-flight: `flight/f4.png`

## README sentences I would add (not written — docs untouched)
- Enterprise row of the views table: "Every defined agent as a node, clustered by division inside a soft nebula in the division's colour; edges are the delegations, verifications and judgements between them. Traffic runs along an edge only while one of its two agents has acted in the last few seconds, coloured by the relationship's kind; with nothing live the edges only breathe. An agent at work wears a turning orbital ring, a certified agent a warm rim and a failed one a dim red rim, and a certificate lands as an expanding ring with a short beam of light. Clicking a node flies the camera to it and drops everything unrelated to three tenths; Esc flies back."
- After the `Esc clears the selection` line: "The enterprise view opens on an establishing shot — the camera starts far out and high above the graph and eases into the resting orbit over two and a half seconds. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` opens it at rest, stops the traffic and the pulsing, and cuts straight to a selected agent instead of flying."

## Shared changes I need (none blocking)
1. **`deck/motion.ts`** — `usePrefersReducedMotion` returns `false` on the first client render, which would paint one frame at the far establishing position before snapping. `CameraRig` therefore reads `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` itself, once, for the opening decision only. If the shell adds a variant with a synchronous first value for `ssr: false` trees, I will drop that local read.
2. **`deck/camera.ts`** — I kept a local `cubicInOut` and a `Shot`/`Flight` pair inside `components/enterprise/CameraRig.tsx`. If shared easing/flight helpers land there, the enterprise rig should adopt them (behaviour is identical: timed cubic ease, lerp of position and `controls.target`).
3. **`deck/store.ts`** — `selectRun` clears `activity` but leaves the `bursts` queue, so a certificate queued under the previous run can draw on the next one. One line (`get().bursts.length = 0`) next to the `activity.clear()` would fix it; the enterprise scene drains whatever is there.
4. **Ops note, not code**: two `next dev` servers against the same `apps/command-deck` directory share one `.next`, which cross-compiles `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL` and breaks both; a production `build` while a dev server runs fails on `/api/fixtures/runs` for the same reason. Run live and replay checks one at a time (this cost me two misleading screenshots).
